title: Label-comprehension and results-interpretation usability assessment instrument for point-of-care G6PD tests
description: A standardized questionnaire developed in line with US FDA guidance on label comprehension studies and WHO Prequalification Technical Specifications Series TSS-2, intended to assess key usability risks and fulfill regulatory evidence requirements. It combines "Thirteen multiple-choice questions with mutually exclusive options and a single correct answer" on label warnings, limitations, restrictions, and procedure with seven short-answer questions on reading, recording, and classifying simulated results. A participant scoring 85% or above was considered to adequately comprehend the test. The instrument has been adapted for training, monitoring, and supervision plans in pilot studies in Bangladesh, Brazil, and the Mekong region.
requirements: Administration with consistent proctoring, as inconsistent instructions and site-varying reminders not to leave blanks may have impacted results
Context-specific adaptation of questions and acceptance criteria to supervisor goals and target users' health literacy and training level
constraints: Designed as a pragmatic tool assessing key aspects of user comprehension only
The modest sample size (n = 45 across 3 countries and 4 sites) does not support robust sub-analyses by site or user type
target_learners: Malaria microscopists, laboratory technicians, nurses, and community health workers who provide malaria case management
target_learning_goals: Comprehension of a point-of-care diagnostic test's intended use, warnings, workflow, and result interpretation
examples: Administered after 2–3 hours of training to 45 health workers in Brazil, Ethiopia, and India, scored unweighted (30 points) and weighted by critical errors (48 points)

title: PATH training materials and simplified quick guides for point-of-care G6PD testing
description: A set of freely available training and job-aid materials supporting the Standard G6PD Test: presentations, a demonstration video, and a competency checklist, available through the G6PD Operational Research Community of Practice. After the usability study, residual risks were addressed through revisions to the IFU and development of "simplified quick guides with workflow clarifications and key safety information" that supplement the IFU and manual, rely primarily on images and simple text easily translated, address common user errors, and include a results-classification table; original art files are available for further iteration.
requirements: Translation and local adaptation to convey key warnings and reinforce proper test procedure in target contexts
constraints: Quick guides are intended to supplement, not replace, the traditional IFU, manual, and other test labelling
target_learners: Diverse intended users of point-of-care G6PD tests, including those with limited education and training
target_learning_goals: Correct test workflow execution, safety awareness, and accurate classification of G6PD results
examples: Quick guides include a table for results classification and were translated into multiple languages
